content:
Hi everyone! I've been working on a project called LeanTEA, a full-stack web framework built entirely in Lean 4, and I'd love to share it with this community.

It ports The Elm Architecture (Model / Msg / update / view) to Lean for both the frontend and the backend. But the main reason I chose Lean 4 wasn't just to write pure functions—it was to explore "Secure by Construction" in a web context.

I wanted to see if we could make classic web vulnerabilities unrepresentable at compile time. Lean's type system made this surprisingly elegant:

  1. Authorization via Dependent Types: Route handlers demand a Proof c argument. To prevent IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference), we use dependent types like Proof (.owner id). The route parameter and the database ownership check must provably agree on the exact id, otherwise the dispatcher won't typecheck.

  2. SQL Injection via Private Constructors: There is no String → SQL path. Queries are built via an AST where the leaf constructors (Where.eq, etc.) are private to the module. You literally cannot concatenate a raw string into a query without getting an Unknown constant error. (We use a decl_name% macro for explicitly audited escapes).

It also bundles MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers. The workflow I'm testing is letting an LLM (Claude) write the route handlers, while the Lean compiler acts as the ultimate, unforgiving security auditor.

If anyone is interested in practical web security, I’d be honored to hear your thoughts or feedback on the design!
Repo: https://github.com/verilean/lean-tea
Docs: https://verilean.github.io/lean-tea

Just a quick review, lean now has an HTTP low level server that your code is not using. Same, HTTP client is on it's way.
I would suggest to migrate to it.

@Alfredo Moreira-Rosa Wow, thanks for the information!
Honestly, I didn't want to maintain a custom HTTP parser long-term.
From a performance and sustainability standpoint, migrating to Lean's upstream low-level HTTP server/client makes perfect sense. Will HTTPS be supported in the future?

https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/tree/master/src/Std/Http/Server
I'll take a look at this. By the way, how do you find APIs?
I know TLS over TCP is on it's way. So i guess HTTPS will follow after that.

https://github.com/Verilean/lean-tea/pull/4
Std.Http.Server suffers from performance degradation under high-frequency access.
lean-tea achieved a 44-fold increase in processing speed by implementing a high-performance backend.

I use Std.Http and don't have those bad performances. My testing show acceptable timings with 15/30ms delays from client request point of view and internal json body processing in nano seconds.
But if course it not nginx level perf, but acceptable compared to node or python.

You can see my implementation LeanIO (inspired by Rust Axum Framework) here :
https://github.com/ecyrbe/leanio
